What is HTML?: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages. It uses tags to structure content. HTML documents form the backbone of every website. An HTML document starts with a DOCTYPE declaration, followed by <html>, <head>, and <body> elements.

Document Structure: Every HTML document has a standard structure. The <!DOCTYPE html> declaration defines the document type. The <html> element wraps all content. Inside <head> we put metadata. Inside <body> we put visible content.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <meta name="description" content="A sample page">
    <title>Document Structure</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
    Visible content goes here.

</body>
</html>
Headings & Paragraphs: HTML provides six levels of headings (<h1> to <h6>) to structure content hierarchically. <h1> is most important, <h6> the least. Paragraphs use <p>. Use <br> for line breaks and <hr> for thematic breaks.

Text Formatting: Use <strong> for importance, <em> for emphasis, <mark> for highlighted text, <small> for fine print, <del> for deleted text, and <ins> for inserted text. Use <sub> for subscript and <sup> for superscript.

Images: The <img> tag embeds images. Required attributes: src (path) and alt (accessibility text). Optional: width, height, loading="lazy". Wrap in <figure>/<figcaption> for captions.
Lists: Three list types: unordered <ul>, ordered <ol>, and description <dl>. List items use <li>. Nested lists go inside <li> elements.

Tables: Tables use <table>, <tr> (row), <th> (header), <td> (data). Group with <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>. Merge cells with colspan and rowspan.
Forms & Inputs: Forms collect user input. The <form> element wraps controls. Common input types: text, password, email, number, checkbox, radio, file, date. Always pair with <label>.

<form action="/submit" method="POST">
    <label for="name">Name:</label>
    <input type="text" id="name" name="name" required>
    <label><input type="checkbox" name="subscribe"> Subscribe</label>
    <select name="country">
        <option value="">Select</option>
        <option value="us">USA</option>
    </select>
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
Block-Level vs Inline Elements: HTML elements are either block-level (start on a new line, take full width) or inline (flow within text). Common block: <div>, <p>, <h1>-<h6>, <section>. Common inline: <span>, <a>, <strong>, <img>. CSS display can change this behavior.

Semantic HTML: Semantic HTML uses meaningful tags: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer>. This improves accessibility, SEO, and code readability.

Audio & Video: Embed media with <audio> and <video>. Use <source> for multiple formats. The controls attribute shows playback UI. Use <track> for subtitles. Supported: MP3, MP4, WebM, OGG.

<audio controls>
    <source src="song.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="song.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
    Browser does not support audio.
</audio>

<video width="640" height="360" controls>
    <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track src="subtitles.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="en">
</video>
Iframes: The <iframe> tag embeds another HTML page. Use sandbox for security, loading="lazy" for deferred loading, and always set title for accessibility.

<iframe src="https://www.example.com" width="800" height="600" title="Example"></iframe>

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" title="YouTube" allowfullscreen sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"></iframe>
SVG Graphics: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is embeddable directly in HTML. Elements: <circle>, <rect>, <path>, <text>, <g>. SVG scales infinitely without quality loss.

<svg width="200" height="200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <rect x="10" y="10" width="180" height="180" rx="10" fill="#4A90D9"/>
    <circle cx="100" cy="80" r="40" fill="#FF6B6B"/>
    <text x="100" y="160" text-anchor="middle" fill="white">SVG</text>
</svg>
Canvas: The <canvas> element provides a drawable region manipulated via JavaScript. Supports 2D graphics, charts, animations, and game rendering. Unlike SVG, canvas is pixel-based.

<canvas id="myCanvas" width="400" height="300"></canvas>
<script>
const c = document.getElementById("myCanvas");
const ctx = c.getContext("2d");
ctx.fillStyle = "#4A90D9";
ctx.fillRect(50, 50, 150, 100);
ctx.fillStyle = "white";
ctx.font = "20px Arial";
ctx.fillText("Canvas", 90, 110);
</script>
Data Attributes: Custom data-* attributes store extra info on elements. Access via JavaScript element.dataset. Useful for storing state or configuration without non-standard attributes.

Picture & Responsive Images: The <picture> element provides responsive images with multiple <source> elements using media queries. Works with srcset for resolution switching.
Embedded Content: Use <object> and <embed> for embedding PDFs, plugins, or legacy content. <param> passes parameters. Modern practice prefers native HTML or iframes.
MathML: MathML marks up mathematical notation using <math> and child elements like <mi>, <mo>, <mfrac>, <msqrt>. Natively supported in modern browsers.

Form Validation: HTML5 validation attributes: required (mandatory), minlength/maxlength (text length), min/max (range), pattern (regex). CSS pseudo-classes :valid/:invalid style states.

Hidden Inputs & Form Security: Hidden inputs (<input type="hidden">) store data not visible to users. Use for CSRF tokens, session IDs, and form state. Security measures: validate server-side, use CSRF tokens, set proper enctype, never trust hidden values.

<form action="/checkout" method="POST">
    <!-- Hidden CSRF token -->
    <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="abc123def456">
    
    <!-- Hidden product data -->
    <input type="hidden" name="product_id" value="9876">
    <input type="hidden" name="price" value="29.99">

    <label>Quantity: <input type="number" name="qty" min="1" value="1"></label>
    <button type="submit">Buy Now</button>
</form>

<!-- Security headers -->
<!-- Meta CSP (set via server ideally) -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'">
Form Attributes Deep Dive: Advanced form attributes: novalidate skips validation, enctype="multipart/form-data" for files, form attribute lets inputs live outside <form>.

<form id="main-form" action="/api/submit" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data" novalidate>
    <input type="file" name="avatar">
</form>
<input type="email" form="main-form">
<input type="submit" form="main-form" value="Submit">

Web Storage: Web Storage API: localStorage (persists across sessions) and sessionStorage (cleared on tab close). Both store key-value pairs as strings. ~5MB per origin.
Geolocation API: Geolocation API accesses user location via navigator.geolocation. getCurrentPosition() for one-time, watchPosition() for tracking. Handle permission denial gracefully.
Drag & Drop API: Drag and Drop API: Set draggable="true" on elements. Events: dragstart, dragover, drop. Use dataTransfer to pass data between drag source and target.

Web Workers: Web Workers run JS in background threads. Communicate via postMessage() / onmessage. Cannot access DOM, window, or parent. Great for CPU-intensive tasks.
Server-Sent Events: Server-Sent Events (SSE) push updates from server to client over HTTP. Use EventSource to subscribe. Simpler than WebSockets for unidirectional data flow.
WebSockets: WebSockets provide full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection. Events: open, message, close, error. Ideal for real-time apps like chat and games.
Fetch API: Fetch API provides promise-based HTTP requests. fetch(url, options) returns a Response promise. Use response.json(), response.text(), or response.blob().
File API & Blobs: File API reads local files via <input type="file"> and FileReader. Blob represents binary data. Use URL.createObjectURL() for file previews.

<input type="file" id="fileInput" multiple accept="image/*">
<script>
document.getElementById("fileInput").onchange = function(e) {
    for (const file of e.target.files) {
        const reader = new FileReader();
        reader.onload = (ev) => {
            const img = document.createElement("img");
            img.src = ev.target.result;
            img.style.maxWidth = "200px";
            document.body.appendChild(img);
        };
        reader.readAsDataURL(file);
    }
};
</script>
IndexedDB: IndexedDB is a browser-based NoSQL database. Stores structured objects with indexes for fast queries. Asynchronous API. Use for complex client-side storage beyond localStorage.
History API: History API manipulates browser session history. pushState() adds entries, replaceState() modifies current. Listen for popstate events. Essential for SPAs.
Web Components: Web Components let you create reusable custom elements. Use customElements.define(), Shadow DOM for encapsulation, <template> for markup, and <slot> for composition.
Service Workers: Service Workers act as proxy between browser and network. Enable offline support, caching, push notifications, and background sync. They run in a separate thread and cannot access DOM.

Semantic Structure Deep Dive: Proper landmark elements: exactly one <main>, one <h1>. Use <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, <footer> for page regions.
Microdata & Structured Data: Microdata adds machine-readable semantics via itemscope, itemtype, itemprop. Schema.org provides vocabulary. Enables rich search results like stars, prices, and recipes.

Performance Optimization: Optimize HTML delivery: use defer for scripts, rel="preload" for critical assets, rel="preconnect" for third-party origins, inline critical CSS. Reduce DOM size and render-blocking resources.

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preload" href="critical.css" as="style">
<script src="app.js" defer></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'">
<noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"></noscript>
Lazy Loading & Hints: Lazy loading defers off-screen resources. Use loading="lazy" on images/iframes. Resource hints: preload (critical), prefetch (future), preconnect (early connection).
WCAG Accessibility: WCAG principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust (POUR). Target WCAG 2.1 AA minimum. Use skip links, proper heading hierarchy, sufficient color contrast, keyboard navigation.

Accessible HTML (ARIA): Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA) attributes supplement HTML semantics for dynamic content and complex UI components. Key ARIA attributes: role (defines element purpose), aria-label (provides an accessible name), aria-labelledby (references another element as label), aria-describedby (references description), aria-hidden (hides from assistive tech), aria-expanded (indicates expandable state), and aria-live (announces dynamic updates). First rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA if you can use native HTML semantics. Use landmark roles like role="navigation" only when the HTML5 equivalent isn't available. Test with screen readers like NVDA, VoiceOver, or JAWS.

HTML Forms Deep Dive: HTML forms collect user input. Essential elements: <form> (container with action/method), <input> (text, email, password, number, date, file, range, color, etc.), <select> and <option> (dropdowns), <textarea> (multi-line text), <fieldset> and <legend> (grouping), <label> (accessibility). Form validation: required, pattern, min/max, minlength/maxlength. novalidate disables browser validation for custom JS validation. Use FormData API for easy data collection. Progressive enhancement: start with a working form, then enhance with JS.

<form id="signup" action="/api/users" method="POST" novalidate>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Personal Information</legend>
    
    <label for="name">Full Name *</label>
    <input type="text" id="name" name="name" required minlength="2" 
           placeholder="John Doe" autocomplete="name">
    
    <label for="email">Email *</label>
    <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required 
           placeholder="john@example.com" autocomplete="email">
    
    <label for="password">Password *</label>
    <input type="password" id="password" name="password" 
           required minlength="8" 
           pattern="(?=.*\d)(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z]).{8,}"
           title="Must contain uppercase, lowercase, and number">
    
    <label for="country">Country</label>
    <select id="country" name="country">
      <option value="">Select...</option>
      <option value="US">United States</option>
      <option value="UK">United Kingdom</option>
      <option value="JP">Japan</option>
    </select>
    
    <label>
      <input type="checkbox" name="terms" required>
      I agree to the terms and conditions
    </label>
  </fieldset>
  
  <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>

<script>
document.getElementById('signup').addEventListener('submit', async (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const data = new FormData(e.target);
  const json = Object.fromEntries(data.entries());
  const resp = await fetch(e.target.action, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(json)
  });
  if (resp.ok) window.location.href = '/welcome';
});
</script>
HTML Multimedia & Embeds: HTML5 provides native multimedia elements: <video>, <audio>, and <picture>. The <video> element supports multiple codecs (MP4/H.264, WebM/VP9, Ogg/Theora) via <source> elements. Attributes: controls, autoplay, loop, muted, poster. The <picture> element enables responsive images with <source media="(...)" srcset="..."> for art direction and resolution switching. <iframe> embeds external content (maps, videos, widgets). Use sandbox for security when embedding untrusted content. The <canvas> element provides bitmap drawing via JavaScript.

Critical Rendering Path: The critical rendering path is the sequence of steps the browser takes to render a page: HTML parsing (DOM), CSS parsing (CSSOM), JavaScript execution (blocking), render tree construction, layout, and paint. Optimize by: deferring non-critical CSS/JS, inlining critical CSS in <head>, using <link rel="preload"> for important resources, and minimizing render-blocking resources. First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measure perceived load speed.

<!-- Critical rendering path optimizations -->
<head>
  <!-- Inline critical CSS -->
  <style>
    body { font-family: system-ui; margin: 0; }
    .hero { display: flex; min-height: 50vh; }
  </style>
  
  <!-- Preload key resources -->
  <link rel="preload" href="font.woff2" as="font" crossorigin>
  <link rel="preload" href="hero.jpg" as="image">
  
  <!-- Defer non-critical CSS -->
  <link rel="preload" href="styles.css" as="style" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'">
  
  <!-- Defer JavaScript -->
  <script src="app.js" defer></script>
  
  <!-- Optimize Largest Contentful Paint -->
  <link rel="preload" href="LCP-image.jpg" as="image" fetchpriority="high">
</head>
SEO Meta Tags & Structured Data: SEO metadata helps search engines understand and rank your content. Essential meta tags: <title> (unique per page, 50-60 chars), <meta name="description"> (150-160 chars), Open Graph tags (Facebook, LinkedIn: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url), Twitter Cards (twitter:card, twitter:site). Structured data using JSON-LD (Schema.org) enhances search results with rich snippets (reviews, recipes, events, FAQs, breadcrumbs). Use Google's Rich Results Test to validate structured data.

<head>
  <!-- Basic SEO -->
  <title>Learn HTML - Complete Tutorial with Examples | Kodex</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Master HTML5 with our comprehensive tutorial covering semantic elements, forms, multimedia, SEO, and best practices. Perfect for beginners and intermediate developers.">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://kodex.dev/html">
  
  <!-- Open Graph -->
  <meta property="og:title" content="Learn HTML - Complete Tutorial">
  <meta property="og:description" content="Master HTML5 with comprehensive tutorials">
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://kodex.dev/og-html.png">
  <meta property="og:type" content="website">
  
  <!-- Twitter Card -->
  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
  <meta name="twitter:site" content="@kodex">
  
  <!-- JSON-LD Structured Data -->
  <script type="application/ld+json">
  {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "Article",
    "headline": "Learn HTML - Complete Tutorial",
    "description": "Master HTML5 with our comprehensive tutorial",
    "author": {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "name": "Kodex"
    },
    "datePublished": "2026-06-10",
    "educationalLevel": "Beginner"
  }
  </script>
</head>

HTML Templates & Slots: The <template> element holds HTML that is not rendered until cloned into the DOM via JavaScript. The <slot> element is used inside web components for content projection — it acts as a placeholder where the parent's light DOM content is inserted. Named slots (slot="name") allow multiple insertion points. Templates are the foundation of reusable web components and are supported in all modern browsers.
